key_insight: For cold-spray additively manufactured 6061 aluminium, FSW showed substantially less macro-porosity and higher local hardness recovery than TIG or MIG under the tested conditions.
engineering_relevance: Welding-process selection and pre-weld heat treatment can improve joint-region quality when joining or repairing CSAM aluminium components.
method: Compared TIG, MIG and FSW in non-heat-treated and heat-treated CSAM 6061 aluminium.
Characterised welded regions using macrographs, micrographs and ImageJ-based porosity analysis.
Measured local hardness using Vickers testing.
evidence_signal: Pre-weld heat treatment reduced 2D pore area fraction from 26.3% to 18.6% for TIG and 30.7% to 22.1% for MIG; hardness recovery relative to corresponding controls was approximately 50–56% for TIG, 63–67% for MIG and 82–84% for FSW.
watch_item: Two-dimensional porosity and local hardness measurements do not establish three-dimensional defect content or joint strength and fatigue performance.
paper_title: A study on porosity formation in cold-spray additively manufactured 6061 aluminium parts using MIG, TIG and FSW welding processes
